quality: AI-assisted demo reference; not independent expert/human gold
routing_policy: Invoke VLM for visible abnormal movement/interaction, or unresolved authorization, visibility or action ambiguity requiring visual/human review. Suppress only explicit confident normal with all risk axes known and low risk. Do not infer routing solely from event name.
limitations: All six clips require visual review; there are no verified normal negative clips. Unnecessary-call rate and normal false-positive rate cannot be measured.
Event spans are conservative visually observed support intervals, not exact onset/offset annotations.
No medical diagnosis, legal authorization or hostile intent is inferred.
SRC04 appears staged against a green backdrop. Physical conflict means observable aggressive physical interaction, including staged demonstrations.
SRC05 is partly occluded; experts should independently adjudicate it before publication.
SRC05/SRC06 are README-referenced views of one incident; no exact synchronization or cross-camera identity is assumed.

SRC01.label: fall_ground_posture
SRC01.observations: Chronological frames show a walking person fall and then remain on the ground. This is observable posture, not a medical collapse diagnosis.
SRC01.routing_rationale: A person transitions from upright movement to persistent ground posture; detection alone cannot determine what happened or required assistance.

SRC02.label: boundary_crossing
SRC02.observations: The person approaches the low brick boundary from outside, climbs across it and moves along the inner path. Authorization is not visible.
SRC02.routing_rationale: A visible boundary-crossing sequence needs visual interpretation; authorization and risk cannot be established from object tracks alone.

SRC03.label: gate_entry_authorization_unknown
SRC03.observations: A red-hat person changes direction, reapproaches the gate, opens/passes the entrance and disappears inside. Permission and intent remain unknown.
SRC03.routing_rationale: Gate entry is visible but authorization is unresolved; route for visual/human review rather than suppressing as ordinary walking or declaring illegal intrusion.

SRC04.label: physical_conflict
SRC04.observations: Four people form two pairs against a green backdrop. Later frames show confrontational raised arms, contact and kicking/punching-style movement. It appears staged; actual hostile intent is unknown.
SRC04.routing_rationale: Physical interaction and aggressive gestures require visual interpretation. A staged setting does not make observable physical interaction normal for this demo ontology.

SRC05.label: physical_conflict
SRC05.observations: Two opposing people at a crossing show raised-arm and lunging/leg movements in sequence, with substantial tree occlusion. This reference is supported by the source's own frames and the README context; many contacts are obscured.
SRC05.routing_rationale: Opposing physical interaction plus partial occlusion is unresolved visual risk. VLM/human review is required even if exact contact cannot be established in an individual frame.

SRC06.label: physical_conflict
SRC06.observations: Chronological frames show opposing arm contact and kicking, a person falling near the parked white vehicle and subsequent standing-over/kicking interaction. The final frame is black.
SRC06.routing_rationale: Direct physical interaction and ground posture require visual interpretation and human review; detector boxes alone cannot safely suppress this incident.
